sources.entry: portkey - Simple web portal that serves as a startup page, displaying a compilation of links and URLs, while also allowing the addition of custom pages, all managed through a single configuration file. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: portkey is a lightweight, self-hosted web portal used as a browser startup page, showing a configurable collection of links with optional custom pages.
summary.what_it_does: portkey serves a single web page listing links (portals) defined in one config.yml file. Portals can be grouped into labelled sections, shown in a multi-column grid, and given emoji, image, or URL icons. A search box supports configurable keywords and optional fuzzy (Levenshtein) matching. Favicons for external links are fetched automatically and can be cached on disk, either fetched directly or relayed through a Vemetric-compatible favicon service. It can also serve small custom HTML pages at configured paths, and includes dark and light modes plus optional Prometheus-style metrics on a separate port.
use_cases: simple intranet or team link portal
how_to_run: Download the portkey binary for your OS and place it in your PATH
Create a config.yml or start from the example configuration in the repository
Start the application with: portkey --config-path=<path to config.yml> (optional if config.yml is in the working directory)
Open your browser at the configured host and port (default localhost:3000)
Docker: docker run --rm -it -v $(PWD)/config.yml:/opt/config.yml -p 3000:3000 codehat/portkey:latest (see README for cache and icon volume options)
notable: All configuration lives in a single config.yml, with environment variable overrides prefixed PORTKEY_
Favicon handling supports direct discovery or a proxied Vemetric-compatible service, with disk caching and a 7-day TTL
Optional Prometheus metrics endpoint with portal, search, and favicon cache counters
Supports custom icon files, emojis, absolute URLs, and data URIs for portal icons
caveats: Favicon caching is disabled by default and requires a writable cache directory when enabled
Custom icon paths in Docker must match the container-side mount point
Custom pages are not added to the portal list automatically and must be listed manually
